ideas.description: Spend part of E069's banked margin on the cheapest time cut found so far: freeze block 1 earlier. Base: E069 (commit 5ed8687; Polar Express NS3 coefficients with output rescaled to NS3's Frobenius norm, bs 1536, 20/28/32 px curriculum at 0-1.5/1.5-3.5/3.5-6.75 epochs, head x2, Muon lr 0.16 mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, jitter, whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only, block 1 frozen from 0.8). Make one change: switch to the existing block-1-frozen graph pair at sample 236250 (0.7 of samples, E061's point) instead of 270000. That pair is the detached block-1 output with the Muon variant without the block-1 groups (now running the Polar Express coefficients), with block-1 BN biases skipped in SGD. Split the straddling step into the two partial shapes, as E061 did. Reuse E061's partial-shape warmups with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035), and confirm that the Polar Express Muon variant without block 1 is warmed at those shapes. Run debug_nan.py and compare trial-0 with later-trial times. Do not anneal block 1 first: E067 showed the anneal adds nothing.
ideas.expected: Time 4.50-4.60 s, point ~4.55 s (-2.8% vs 4.678 s, as in E061 vs E058). Accuracy 0.7520-0.7575, point ~0.7550 (E069 0.7561 minus E061's paired cost of -0.11 pp, which held on both seeds 0-2 and seeds 3-12). Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep, new best. Infeasible by <=0.05 pp: keep the code path for the stack idea. A drop >=0.3 pp means Polar Express made late block-1 updates more valuable; then close earlier freezing at 0.8.

ideas.description: Retry E054's near-miss on the margin E069 banked. Base: E069 (commit 5ed8687). Make one change: move the 28 -> 32 px switch from 3.5 to 4.0 epochs (sample 200000), so 28 px runs epochs 1.5-4.0 (still without translate) and 32 px with translate-2 runs 4.0-6.75. Total epochs, bs, the sample stream, the block-1 freeze at 0.8 (sample 270000) and every sample-indexed schedule stay unchanged. Port the switch logic from E054 (commit 81c1232) and split the straddling step into the two partial shapes. In build(), warm up the new partial shapes at sample 200000 for the 28 px and 32 px graphs with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Keep build under ~450 s. Run debug_nan.py on the new shapes and compare trial-0 with later-trial times.
ideas.expected: Time 4.52-4.62 s, point ~4.57 s (-2.3% vs 4.678 s, as in E054 vs E052). Accuracy 0.7505-0.7570, point ~0.7539 (E069 minus E054's -0.22 pp). Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep. Since E054's single paired point sits at 0.1 pp per 1%, a drop >=0.35 pp means the 32 px tail floor is ~3.25 epochs; then refute H6.3.1 and close stage-length tuning.

ideas.description: Now that Polar Express coefficients whiten more per iteration, test whether 2 of them can replace the tip's 3. Base: E069. Make one change inside both batched compiled Muon variants: run 2 NS iterations with coefficients from optimal_composition(num_iters=2, l=ℓ) (arxiv 2505.16932), with ℓ the same 5th-percentile ratio E069 measured, the published safety scaling, and no truncation of a longer list. Then rescale each group's output to the same per-group Frobenius target E069 uses, so the step size is unchanged. Gate in drafts/ on real seed-0 momentum matrices at steps 1/100/end: launch only if (a) the fraction of normalized singular values >0.5 after NS2-PE is >= 86% (the old fixed-coefficient NS3 level, i.e. no weaker than E058's whitening, because E065 showed weaker whitening falls off a cliff), (b) the max singular value is <= 1.3, and (c) drafts/time_muon.py shows a saving >= 0.3 ms/step. Re-warm both Muon variants in build() and run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs.
ideas.expected: If the gate passes: time 4.58-4.63 s, point ~4.60 s (-1.6%; one of three NS iterations is ~0.37 ms of the ~1.13 ms NS cost, over ~221 steps). Accuracy 0.7505-0.7570, point ~0.7545 (between E058's whitening level and E069's). Feasible and >=1.2% faster with a pre-measured deterministic saving: keep (E051 precedent). A drop >=0.25 pp means the E069 gain needs all 3 iterations; then refute H2.4.6. If the gate fails, retire H2.4.6 without a run.

ideas.description: Push whitening strength one step further at zero cost. E065 (-1.51 pp, weaker) and E069 (+0.24 pp, stronger) both say accuracy rises with whitening strength around the default. Base: E069. Make one change: recompute the 3 Polar Express triples with optimal_composition(num_iters=3, l=ℓ'), where ℓ' is the 0.5th-percentile smallest-singular-value ratio (or ℓ/4 if that is smaller) instead of the 5th percentile. This lifts the smallest singular directions harder, at some cost in precision near 1. Keep the safety scaling and the per-group Frobenius rescale to E069's target, so only the spectrum shape changes. Gate in drafts/ on seed-0 momentum matrices at steps 1/100/end: the fraction of singular values >0.5 must be >= 98% (E069: ~95%), and the max singular value must be <= 1.3. Retire without a run if no ℓ' meets both. Re-warm both Muon variants and run debug_nan.py.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.20 to +0.30 pp, point +0.07 pp (~0.7568). Time unchanged (±0.5%, same bmm count). A gain >=0.15 pp supports a monotone whitening-strength picture; keep it and bank margin for the freeze/28 px stack. Within ±0.12 pp: whitening is saturated at ~95% lifted, so close H1.2.7 and the H1 update branch.

ideas.description: Combine the two margin-funded time cuts. Run only after the freeze-at-0.7 and 28px-to-4.0 ideas on E069 have both been read, and only if each was feasible or infeasible by <=0.05 pp, with a summed accuracy drop vs E069 of <=0.28 pp. Base: the faster of those two commits if it was kept, else E069. Make one change: add the other cut, so block 1 freezes at sample 236250 AND the 28 -> 32 px switch is at sample 200000. Every other setting and the sample-indexed schedules stay unchanged. Warm up every partial shape at both switches for the unfrozen and frozen 32 px graphs and the 28 px graph, with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Run debug_nan.py and compare trial-0 with later-trial times.
ideas.expected: Time 4.40-4.50 s, point ~4.44 s (-5% vs E069; the two cuts touch different stages and should be roughly additive). Accuracy 0.7500-0.7560, point ~0.7530 (borderline; additive costs -0.11 and -0.22 pp). Feasible: keep, new best. Infeasible by <=0.05 pp: keep whichever single cut was kept and wait for the next accuracy gain (the stronger-whitening idea). A combined drop larger than the sum of the single drops by >=0.15 pp means the cuts interact, with fewer full-res unfrozen block-1 steps; then stop stacking.

Pair it against the existing E058 seeds 3-12 results in drafts/extra_seeds (mean 0.75328, same seeds and harness). Report per-seed accuracy, the mean, the paired per-seed differences and their sd, and per-trial train time. Record the result as evidence for H1.2.7, and for H4.1.2 on the new tip.

Prediction: E069 extra-seed mean 0.7545-0.7565, point ~0.7553; paired E069 - E058 on seeds 3-12 +0.10 to +0.30 pp, point +0.2; paired per-seed sd ~0.2-0.25 pp. If the extra-seed mean is >=0.7545, run the time-cut stack as planned. ideas.description: Explore the low side of the Muon lr on the new whitening. Polar Express lifts ~95% of singular directions against ~86% for the old NS3, and the output is rescaled to the old Frobenius norm, so the per-direction rotation is smaller and spread more evenly. The lr optimum may have moved. Base: E069. A gain >=0.15 pp means the stronger whitening wants smaller rotations: keep it, and the follow-up is 0.09. Within ±0.12 pp: the Muon lr axis is flat over 0.12-0.24, so close H1.2.4 as supported. A drop >=0.25 pp means 0.16 is near the lower edge of the optimum; close the axis.

A drop >=0.25 pp means block 2 depends on block 1's batch-stat noise; refute H7.2.1. A saving <0.7% means the BN stat work is already fused into neighbouring kernels; close H7.2.

structured_output.summary:
There were no queued ideas left (everything was done or dropped), so I wrote 8 new ones and dropped none. The tip is E069: Polar Express coefficients, 0.7561 at 4.678 s, which clears the 0.753 gate by 0.31 pp. The plan spends that margin on near-misses that were previously infeasible.

Exploit ideas:
- **Freeze block 1 at 0.7 on E069** (H2.4.7, priority 5). E061 measured -2.8% time for -0.11 pp, the same on seeds 0-2 and on seeds 3-12. Expect ~4.55 s at ~0.7550.
- **28 px stage to 4.0 epochs on E069** (H6.3.1, priority 4). E054 measured -2.3% for -0.22 pp. Expect ~4.57 s at ~0.7539.
- **Stack both cuts** (priority 3, conditional on the two single reads). Expect ~4.44 s at ~0.7530, borderline.
- **Two Polar Express iterations instead of three** (H2.4.6, priority 3). Launch only if the gates pass: whitening must be no weaker than the old NS3 (E065 cliff) and the saving must be at least 0.3 ms/step. Expect -1.6% time.

Diagnostic:
- **Offline check of E069 on seeds 3-12** (priority 4), paired against the existing E058 results on the same seeds. This confirms whether the +0.24 pp gain is real before the margin is spent.

Explore ideas:
- **Stronger whitening at zero cost** (H1.2.7, priority 3): lower ℓ so at least 98% of singular values are lifted. Expect about +0.07 pp.
- **Muon lr 0.12 on the new whitening** (H1.2.4, priority 2). Expect about -0.05 pp.
- **Eval-mode BN in the frozen block 1** (H7.2.1, priority 1). Expect about -0.9% time.

Closed axes are not reproposed: label targets, the SGD group, averaging, batch size, epoch trimming (E070), block-2 freezing, and weaker or uniformized Muon updates.
